name: QRC Image
description: Train a quantum reservoir on a sequence of images (or continue one already trained) and generate a new sequence, rendered as an animated GIF.

output_files.name: state
output_files.description: Advanced reservoir state; reuse on a later call as job:<id>/state.

fps.description: Frames per second for the generated GIF.
fps.title: Fps

periodic.description: Allow training windows to wrap past the end of `training_sequence` back to the start, treating it as cyclic. Used only when training (state is absent); ignored otherwise.
periodic.title: Periodic

quality.description: Training effort, used only when training (i.e. `state` is absent): fast is quick and rough, complete trains longest on the most data.
quality.title: Quality

seed.description: Top-level RNG seed for training. Used only when training (state is absent); None picks a random seed for this run, recorded in the returned state so the exact run can be reproduced later by passing it back explicitly. Ignored when continuing from a state — its own build seed is always reused, since a different value would reconstruct a different physical reservoir than the one the readout was trained against.
seed.title: Seed

training_sequence.description: Sequence of filenames from `vocabulary`, in training order. Required when `state` is not given (there's nothing yet to continue from); ignored otherwise.
training_sequence.title: Training Sequence

variation.description: Sampling temperature: low = deterministic/repetitive, high = random
variation.title: Variation

description_md:
qrc-image-v1 — train (once) or continue a quantum reservoir over a vocabulary of images, and
render the generated token sequence back into an animated GIF.

The vocabulary is a zip of images: each image's filename is itself a token, so
qrc.data.sequence_mapping.SequenceMapping can build its index straight from the zip's filenames
and `training_sequence` is just a list of those filenames in training order. This engine maps the
generated filenames back to image bytes to build the GIF.

Two paths, chosen by whether `state` is given:
  - no `state` -> train a fresh reservoir on `training_sequence` (quality picks epochs/sample_fraction).
  - `state` given -> skip training, reload the trained reservoir/readout from it and keep going.

Either way it then generates `length` frames and returns the GIF as the primary output, with the
new state and the vocabulary zip riding alongside as named files — `files.state` and
`files.vocabulary` — so a later call can reference both by job id instead of re-uploading/re-training
(see named-output references, `job:<id>/<name>`, in the platform's v0.6 protocol).

code_samples.source:
import requests
BASE = "https://api.mothquantum.com/v1"
HEADERS = {"Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_KEY"}

# First call: no state yet -> trains, then generates once.
r = requests.post(
    f"{BASE}/generation/qrc-image-v1/process",
    headers=HEADERS,
    files={"vocabulary": open("images.zip", "rb")},
    data={
        "training_sequence": ["a.png", "b.png", "c.png", "a.png"],
        "length": 10,
        "quality": "moderate",
    },
)
job_id = r.json()["job_id"]
# ... poll GET {BASE}/status/{job_id} until "completed" ...

gif_bytes = requests.get(f"{BASE}/result/{job_id}", headers=HEADERS).content
open("generated.gif", "wb").write(gif_bytes)

# Generate more from the same trained reservoir — no re-upload, no re-train. `state` and
# `vocabulary` are this job's own named outputs, referenced by id (no separate download/upload).
r = requests.post(
    f"{BASE}/generation/qrc-image-v1/process",
    headers=HEADERS,
    data={
        "length": 20,
        "vocabulary": f"job:{job_id}/vocabulary",
        "state": f"job:{job_id}/state",
    },
)

curl -X POST https://api.mothquantum.com/v1/generation/qrc-image-v1/process \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_KEY" \
  -F vocabulary=@images.zip \
  -F 'training_sequence=["a.png","b.png","c.png","a.png"]' \
  -F length=10
# ... poll GET /v1/status/{job_id} until "completed", then:
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_KEY" https://api.mothquantum.com/v1/result/{job_id} -o generated.gif
